title: Native resolver compatibility stabilization

trigger.observed_behavior: Network-enabled Bubblewrap commands could reach direct IP HTTPS but hostname requests failed at DNS resolution.
trigger.sandbox_fact: /etc/resolv.conf was a symlink whose /run/systemd/resolve target was absent inside the sandbox.
trigger.permission_fact: Granting the existing network permission did not repair DNS, proving the defect was mount compatibility rather than an authorization denial.

scope: Preserve a trusted host resolver target with one read-only file bind when required.
Keep /run broadly hidden and safe-mode networking unshared.
Add fail-closed unit and target evidence for supported and unsafe resolver targets.
Rerun real hostname/web access without resolver workarounds.
non_goals: No workflow, OAuth, MCP, state-schema, public-tool or finalizer change.
No broad /run mount or arbitrary symlink-target mount.
No DNS-over-HTTPS fallback or embedded resolver.
No unrelated Native refactor or performance claim.
security_invariants: Only an explicitly trusted regular resolver file may be mounted outside existing system roots.
Private vault, home secrets and unrelated /run service state remain hidden.
The resolver mount is read-only and creates no new production authority.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first resolver-mount draft applied only to Dangerous mode even though Trusted mode also shares the host network namespace and would therefore have retained the same dangling resolver defect.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Treat both Trusted and Dangerous as network-enabled modes for the narrowly scoped resolver-file bind, keep Safe mode excluded and --unshare-net, and add real Trusted and Dangerous DNS/HTTPS checks.

recorded_failures_and_repairs.failure: The first target script proved that helper processes exited but did not yet measure repeated-request fd/thread non-growth, which was insufficient for the declared A5 boundary.
recorded_failures_and_repairs.repair: Add a twenty-request resource non-regression check requiring zero helper-process growth, zero thread growth, bounded fd delta and no performance claim.

commands.command: cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy -p mtm-native --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test -p mtm-native
commands.result: Native targeted gate passed with twelve unit tests, including trusted regular-file/symlink handling, unsafe target rejection and proof that no broad /run bind is emitted.

Real Bubblewrap target passed seven security/resource checks and ten real-web cases without resolver workarounds; Trusted and Dangerous hostname HTTPS both returned 200 while Safe remained network-isolated.

commands.command: cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace && python3 scripts/validate_migration_graph.py && python3 scripts/validate_engineering_graph.py && python3 scripts/run_checks.py && git diff --check
commands.result: The complete workspace, architecture/migration governance, unified local validation and diff hygiene passed with the resolver change present.

manual_pending: Other Linux distributions or resolver managers whose /etc/resolv.conf targets differ from the approved runtime prefixes require their own target qualification.
Packaging this source into the next MTM preview/final release remains part of release qualification and does not change MTM-010's source-level acceptance.
rollback: Revert only the resolver-file mount change and retain the accepted prior Native sandbox mount set.
